The geographical area that was analyzed for socio-economic impacts includes all of Big Horn County with the exception of the southeastern corner. The Busby-Decker Census Division in the southeastern corner of the county was excluded because:
(1) it is geographically separated by the Wolf and Rosebud mountains;
(2) it is already impacted by the Decker mine and;
(3) it includes virtually no Crow Indians and in fact contains a significant portion of the Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation.
There is little social or economic interaction between the Decker

Area and the rest of the county so a much more accurate picture of
\nimpending and projected impacts in the Westmoreland Resources Project

Area can be obtained by isolating the two areas. The area which will be

most heavily impacted is shown on Map II-5.
There will also be limited impacts on the area bordering the Yellowstone River, particularly the town of Hysham (1970 population 373) which is only slightly farther from the Westmoreland site than Hardin. Facilities in the Hysham area are very limited and it is felt that unless cumulative impacts are extreme, this area will be relatively unaffected by the proposed project. However, possible impacts on the Hysham area are described in this report.
Big Horn County as a whole contains a substantial number of Northern Cheyenne Indians, who will probably not be impacted in any significant way by coal development in the Crow Ceded Area. By defining the impact area so as to consider mainly the Crow Indian population of Big Horn County, the socio-economic impact analysis is both less complex and more reliable.
